meta: You type a question on your phone, but the AI isn't inside your phone. It lives very far away. Big AI models run in data centers full of GPUs, reached through an API. Plus: regions, autoscaling and on-device AI.

muc.title: AI is very far away
muc.text: You type a question on your phone, but the AI isn't inside your phone. It's very far away.

muc.title: AI's building
muc.text: Big AI models run in data centers: buildings full of server racks with GPUs, a special kind of chip. They use as much power as a whole neighborhood, and need constant cooling.

muc.title: A door called an API
muc.text: Apps send your question over the internet to that building, through a door called an API, and get the answer back. Most AI apps don't run their own models. They rent them through this door, as video 56 explained.

muc.title: Which country your data is in
muc.text: Which region the data center is in, meaning which country, matters too. Banks and hospitals often have to choose where their data lives because of regulations.

muc.title: Overloaded, try again later
muc.text: At peak hours, millions of people ask at once. The system turns on more machines by itself, called autoscaling. If it can't keep up, you see the familiar message: overloaded, try again later.

muc.title: AI right on your phone
muc.text: There are also small models that run right on your phone, called on-device AI. No internet needed, your data never leaves the device, but they're less smart. Many new phones use both: light tasks on the phone, hard ones sent to the cloud.

muc.title: Check the status page
muc.text: Next time AI is slow or shows an error, don't ask ten times. Search the app's name plus the word status, open the company's status page, and see if there's an outage.

muc.title: The door needs a guard
muc.text: With AI that far away, the door needs a guard. Part three: input guardrails.
